vulnerabilities.description: Session context and metrics stored in plaintext JSON files without encryption. Sensitive data in .claude-flow/sessions/ directory is unencrypted and could be read if filesystem is compromised.
Memory data stored in plaintext JSON at .claude-flow/data/memory.json. No encryption of potentially sensitive key-value pairs. File permissions not explicitly restricted.
File descriptor access to .swarm/memory.db and .claude/memory.db via fs.statSync without permission checks. Database files may contain sensitive patterns and learning data.
Potential race condition: mkdir with recursive option followed by file writes. If filesystem is concurrent, files could be created with overly permissive defaults.

recommendations: Encrypt sensitive session data before storing to disk. Use authenticated encryption (AES-256-GCM) for .claude-flow/sessions/ directory with a key derived from environment or secure storage.
Restrict file permissions on memory.json and database files to user-only read/write (mode 0600). Use fs.writeFileSync with {mode: 0o600} flag.
Add explicit file permission checks or use a secrets manager for any future authentication tokens or API credentials.
For the statusline.js database estimates, validate that paths exist and are regular files before accessing stats—add fs.lstatSync checks.
Add try-catch error handling in reset-project.js for file system operations with explicit error logging.
Command injection mitigated properly ✓ (execFileSync with shell: false)
